summary: Donna Lynn Brown works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned degrees from the University of Manitoba and Maitripa College, later serving as an associate editor for the FPMT (2016–2017) and sessional instructor at Manitoba (2023).
Donna Strahan is a specialist in history and archaeology. She was a conservator at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (attested 2010) and became Head at the National Museum of Asian Art in 2014.

Dor Bahadur Bista, working in Tibetology, studied at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus and founded the Karnali Institute. He served on the board of ICIMOD (~1984) and was a professor at Tribhuvan University (~1975–1993).
Doranne Jacobson is an Indologist who earned a doctorate in anthropology from Columbia University. She later served as a seminar associate at Columbia's Southern Asian Institute.

Doris Meth Srinivasan works in Indology, religious studies, and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, held posts at George Mason and George Washington universities, and curated at Nelson-Atkins Museum.
Doris Unterthurner is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her MA at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Dorje Rinchen (1819–1867) was an expert in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Sakya Yab Jé Kün Ga Rinchen, Chime Tenpai Nyima, and Sakya Dak Chen Ngawang Kün Ga Gyaltsen, and taught Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Dorje Tseten (1925–2013) worked in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied education at Beijing Normal University (~1944–1948) and served as director of the China Tibetology Research Center from 1986 to 2000.

Dorji Banzarov (1822–1855) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at the First Kazan Male Gymnasium and Kazan Imperial University (~1842–1846), completing his doctoral dissertation under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski.

Dorji Penjore works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD in anthropology from the Australian National University (2012–2016) and served at the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH and the Royal Institute of Management.

Dorji Wangchuk specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, becoming a professor at Hamburg in 1998.

Dorothy C. Wong specializes in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She earned degrees from International Christian University, CUHK, and Harvard University (PhD 1995), later joining the University of Virginia and visiting the University of Hong Kong (2009).
Dorothy Maskell (d. 1956) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. Succeeding William Stede, she served as Reader of Pāli at SOAS University of London from 1949 to 1956.
Dory Heilijgers is an Indologist who served as librarian of the Kern Institute at Leiden University (attested 1999) and held an affiliation there attested in 2008.

Douglas Allen is a philosopher of religion who studied at Yale, Banaras Hindu, and Vanderbilt universities. He taught at Southern Illinois and Central Connecticut State before becoming a professor and Professor Emeritus of Philosophy at the University of Maine.

Douglas Barrett (1917–1992) was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He studied classics at the University of Oxford and attended SOAS, later serving as a curator at the British Museum (1969–1977).

Douglas Craven Phillott (1860–1930) worked in linguistics, Indology, and history and archaeology. Educated at Felsted School and Sandhurst, he was a Fellow of The Asiatic Society and lecturer in Urdu and Hindustani at Gonville and Caius College.

Douglas Gildow specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Princeton University under Stephen F. Teiser and Qi Zhou, later teaching at Florida State and The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Douglas J. Penick is an author in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Princeton University (~1962–1966) and trained under traditional teacher Chögyam Trungpa in 1971.

Douglas L. Berger works in philosophy, Sinology, and Indology. He served as assistant professor of philosophy at Southern Illinois University Carbondale and later became professor and director of the Centre for Intercultural Philosophy at Leiden University.
